function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

**Paris – Quick Snapshot**

| Topic | Details |
|-------|---------|
| **Location** | Capital city of France, situated in the Île-de-France region along the Seine River. |
| **Population** | ~2.1 million residents in the city proper; ~12 million in the greater metropolitan area. |
| **Area** | 105 km² (city proper). |
| **Language** | French (official). |
| **Time Zone** | Central European Time (CET, UTC+1); Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in daylight saving months. |
| **Key Landmarks** | Eiffel Tower, Louvre Museum, Notre-Dame Cathedral, Arc de Triomphe, Sacré‑Coeur, Musée d’Orsay, Palais Garnier, Champs‑Élysées. |
| **Transportation** | Extensive metro, RER commuter rail, buses, trams, bike‑share (Vélib’), major airports (Charles de Gaulle, Orly). |
| **Cuisine Highlights** | Croissants, baguettes, escargot, coq au vin, macarons, cheese varieties (brie, camembert), wine from nearby regions. |
| **Culture & Events** | Fashion Week (Fall/Winter & Spring/Summer), Paris Film Festival, Bastille Day celebrations, numerous art galleries, cafés, literary cafés. |
| **Economy** | Hub for finance, fashion, luxury goods, tech startups, tourism, and international diplomacy (UN agencies, UNESCO). |
| **Climate** | Oceanic climate: mild winters (~3–7 °C), warm summers (~18–25 °C), moderate rainfall year‑round. |

---

### Quick Tips for Visitors

| Tip | Why |
|-----|-----|
| **Buy a Paris Pass** | Saves on entry fees to many museums and offers unlimited metro rides. |
| **Explore Lesser‑Known Neighborhoods** | Le Marais, Canal Saint‑Martin, Belleville, and Montmartre offer authentic vibes beyond the main tourist spots. |
| **Try Local Markets** | Marché d’Aligre, Marché des Enfants Rouges, and Marché Bastille for fresh produce, cheeses, and street food. |
| **Use Public Transport** | Metro is fast and covers most attractions; consider a multi‑day pass. |
| **Plan for Crowds** | Visit major sites early in the morning or late afternoon to avoid peak crowds. |
| **Stay Hydrated & Wear Comfortable Shoes** | Paris involves a lot of walking, especially around historic districts. |

---

If you have a specific question—whether it’s about travel planning, history, culture, or anything else—just let me know!
